thread.title: Universal Display Stock Falls As OLED Market 'Takes A Breather'

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Universal Display Stock Falls As OLED Market 'Takes A Breather'
text:
Shares of Universal Display ( OLED ), a key player in the OLED display market, tumbled Friday after the company signaled a slowdown ahead in the transition to organic light-emitting diode displays.
X Universal Display stock plunged 15.8% to close at 130.40 on the stock market today . It stabbed below its 200-day moving average line, a critical support level. Just five weeks ago, the stock hit a record high of 209.
The Ewing, N.J.-based company late Thursday reported better-than-expected December-quarter results , but guided to 2018 sales well below views. Universal Display expects revenue in the range of $350 million to $380 million this year, vs. Wall Street expectations for $400 million.
On a conference call with analysts, Universal Display Chief Executive Steve Abramson said OLED manufacturing growth will "take a bit of a breather this year" as companies gear up for 2019 product cycles.
"In the consumer electronics landscape, from small screens to large screens, the adoption of bright, beautiful, brilliant OLED technology continues to grow," Abramson said. New products include Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone X, Samsung's upcoming Galaxy S9 smartphone and big-screen OLED televisions from LG Electronics, he said.
"The increasing pipeline of customers' activity is indicative of the OLED industry's momentum from expanding OLED development and commercial activity to new OLED capacity plans," he said.
